sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Pippa. Are you good at saving money, Neil?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是皮帕,你很会存钱吗?

sentences.en: Or do you like to spend it? Well, actually, a bit of both.
sentences.zh: 或者你喜欢花它?

sentences.en: I like to spend money on nice things, but I also try to save, mainly because I've got children.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把钱花在好东西上, 但我也试图储蓄, 主要是因为我有孩子。

sentences.en: How about you? Yeah, I'm the same. I like to save money, or I try to, for the future.
sentences.zh: 是的,我也是,我喜欢为未来存钱

sentences.en: But I also do spend it. I don't count every penny that I spend and save every single penny that I earn.
sentences.zh: 但我也花光了它。我不计算我花的每一分钱 并保存我赚的每一分钱。

sentences.en: Mmm. Well, whether you're a saver or a spender, being in debt is common in the UK.
sentences.zh: 无论是储蓄者还是支出者 债务在英国是常见的

sentences.en: Debt refers to money a person has borrowed to buy something and which they have to pay back, usually to a bank, a credit card company, or another person.
sentences.zh: 债务是指一个人借来买东西的钱,他们必须偿还,通常还给银行、信用卡公司或其他人。

sentences.en: Many people avoid talking about debt, but it affects us all.
sentences.zh: 许多人避免谈论债务,但它影响到我们所有人。

sentences.en: In 2025, over 1000 people contacted the UK Citizens Advice Bureau every single day of the year for help with their debt.
sentences.zh: 2025年,每年每天有1 000多人与联合王国公民咨询局联系,以帮助他们偿还债务。

sentences.en: And when debt gets out of control, it causes stress and worry.
sentences.zh: 当债务失控时 就会引起压力和担忧

sentences.en: BBC Radio 4 programme Thinking Allowed interviewed one young man, Jason, about his debt.
sentences.zh: 英国广播公司第四电台节目 " 认为允许 " 采访了一位年轻人,Jason, 谈到他的债务。

sentences.en: Whatever jobs there are aren't enough to provide for a family.
sentences.zh: 不管有什么工作 都不足以养家糊口

sentences.en: Sometimes you need to take out loans. I've done it a few times, but you can't ever pay it back.
sentences.zh: 有时你需要贷款,我做过几次,但你永远还不了

sentences.en: You can't see a way out, other than winning the lottery or something.
sentences.zh: 除了中彩票什么的 你看不到出路

sentences.en: I'd like to think I could clear them all one day, even if it means, like, five years paying them off.
sentences.zh: 我想,我可以 清理他们所有一天, 即使这意味着一样,五年 支付他们。

sentences.en: Jason uses three phrases, pay back, pay off, and clear debt, all of which mean the same thing – to give back the money you've borrowed.
sentences.zh: Jason用了三个词,还钱,还债,还债, 都意味着同样的事情—— 把钱还给你。

sentences.en: In this episode, we'll hear more about living with debt by learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 在这集里,我们将会通过学习一些有用的新词句 来听到更多关于债务生活的故事。

sentences.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary used, plus a quiz and worksheet, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 并记住,你会发现所有使用的词汇, 加上一个测验和工作表, 在我们的网站上,bbc学习英语.com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Pippa.
sentences.zh: 但首先 我有一个问题要问你 皮帕

sentences.en: According to debt support group The Money Charity, roughly how much is the average British adult in debt through credit cards, overdrafts and personal loans?
sentences.zh: 根据债务支助团体 " 金钱慈善 " 的说法,英国成年人通过信用卡、透支和个人贷款承担债务的平均数大约是多少?

sentences.en: Hmm. I'm not sure. I'll say £2,200. OK. Well, we will find out the answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我不知道,我说2200英镑 好吧,我们稍后在节目中会找出答案

sentences.en: Jason's story features in a new book by sociologist Ryan Davey.
sentences.zh: Jason的故事在社会学家Ryan Davey的一本新书里特别报道

sentences.en: Ryan spent months living in a low-income housing estate, which he gave the fictional name Woldham.
sentences.zh: 瑞安住在一个低收入的房产里几个月 他给这个小说取名为沃尔德姆

sentences.en: He talked with residents and listened to their money worries.
sentences.zh: 他与居民交谈,并听取了他们对钱的担忧。

sentences.en: Here, Ryan explains more to BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed: My approach was to let people know that I was interested in learning about their lives and how they were making ends meet, so I did some interviews with residents, and I paid attention to where debt came up in everyday conversations.
sentences.zh: Ryan向BBC电台4的“思想允许”解释更多:我的方法是让人们知道, 我有兴趣了解他们的生活以及他们如何维持生计,

sentences.en: For many people in Woldham, Jason included, debt was an ordinary feature of daily life.
sentences.zh: 对沃尔德姆的许多人来说,包括杰森在内,债务是日常生活的一个普通特征。

sentences.en: And beyond that, being in arrears – so, being behind with one or more monthly payment commitments – was part of daily life.
sentences.zh: 此外,拖欠会费——因此,拖欠一个或一个以上月的付款承诺——是日常生活的一部分。

sentences.en: The people of Woldham were making ends meet.
sentences.zh: 沃尔德姆的人民正在维持生计。

sentences.en: To make ends meet means having just enough money to pay for basic living expenses like food, bills and rent.
sentences.zh: 维持生计意味着有足够的钱支付基本生活费用,如食物、账单和房租。

sentences.en: Ryan found that many residents were in arrears, a phrase meaning to still owe money that should have already been repaid.
sentences.zh: 瑞安发现许多居民都拖欠钱款,

sentences.en: For most residents, debt was a normal part of daily life.
sentences.zh: 对大多数居民来说,债务是日常生活的正常部分。

sentences.en: With a regular income, debt can be managed, but for those who are unemployed or on low incomes, it can cause serious distress.
sentences.zh: 有了正常收入,就可以管理债务,但对那些失业或低收入的人来说,债务可能会造成严重的困扰。

sentences.en: Here, Ryan discusses how the residents he met felt about their debt with BBC Radio 4's Thinking Allowed: Jason actually fluctuated between wanting to clear all of his debts on the one hand, and on the other what he described as living on the never-never and actually questioning the supposed moral obligation to pay his debts.
sentences.zh: 瑞安在这里讨论他遇到的居民对英国广播公司第四电台的“思想允许”的债务的感受:杰森实际上在想清清所有债务与他所说的永无休止的生活之间起伏不定,实际上质疑所谓的偿还债务的道德义务。

sentences.en: Over the months that I knew him, the financial strain on him and his partner increased.
sentences.zh: 在我认识他的几个月里, 他和他的搭档的经济压力增加了。

sentences.en: They missed some of their bills. Their internet was disconnected.
sentences.zh: 他们错过了一些账单 他们的互联网被切断了

sentences.en: Jason was living on the never-never, an informal phrase for buying the things you need by making regular small payments over a long time.
sentences.zh: Jason一直生活在一个从未有过的, 一个非正式的短语 购买你需要的东西 通过定期 小额支付 很长一段时间。

sentences.en: It's called the never-never because it seems the debt will never be repaid.
sentences.zh: 这叫永不偿还 因为债务似乎永远无法偿还

sentences.en: Jason experienced financial strain – emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet his basic needs or to repay his debt.
sentences.zh: Jason经历了财政紧张 — — 缺乏满足其基本需求或偿还其债务所需的资金造成了情绪压力。

sentences.en: Debt is a serious issue. It affects many people and there are support groups who can help if you need it.
sentences.zh: 债务是一个严重的问题,它影响到许多人,如果需要的话,也有支持团体可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: OK. Neil, what was the answer to your question?
sentences.zh: 尼尔,你的问题的答案是什么?

sentences.en: I asked what the average amount of debt a British adult has through credit cards, overdrafts and personal loans.
sentences.zh: 我问一个英国成年人通过信用卡、透支和个人贷款的平均债务数额。

sentences.en: I said it was around £2,200. I'm afraid that's not the right answer.
sentences.zh: 我说了大约2200英镑 恐怕这答案不对

sentences.en: In fact, it's £4,232. OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with debt – money a person has borrowed and needs to give back.
sentences.zh: 事实上,这是4,232英镑。让我们回顾一下我们学到的词汇,首先从债务开始 — — 一个人借了需要还的钱。

sentences.en: The phrases to pay back, to pay off, and to clear a debt all mean to give back money you have borrowed.
sentences.zh: 偿还债务 偿还债务 偿还债务 都意味着还回你借的钱

sentences.en: If someone is making ends meet, they have just enough money to pay for basic living expenses.
sentences.zh: 如果有人在维持生计,他们就有足够的钱支付基本生活费用。

sentences.en: And if they are in arrears, they still owe money that should have been repaid already.
sentences.zh: 如果他们拖欠,他们仍欠着本该还清的钱。

sentences.en: If you buy something on the never-never, you buy it by making small regular payments over a long period.
sentences.zh: 如果你买的东西从来没有, 你买它 通过小定期支付 很长一段时间。

sentences.en: And finally, financial strain is emotional stress caused by a lack of money to meet your basic needs.
sentences.zh: 最后,财政紧张是由于缺乏满足基本需要的资金而造成的情绪压力。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to know how debt is spelled and all the other words from this episode, visit our website, bbclearningenglish.com, to find a full vocabulary list.
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟到了, 但如果你想知道债务是如何拼写 和所有其他词 从这集,访问我们的网站,bbclearingenglish.com, 找到一个完整的词汇列表。

sentences.en: See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见,但现在再见了

sentences.en: Bye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
